headline: 五, “five”, comes from Middle Chinese (MC nguX).
コード traces to three English words: “code”, “cord” and “chord”.
首, “neck”, is from Old Japanese, from Proto-Japonic *kunpi.
スケジュール is borrowed from English “schedule”.
碗, “bowl”, is a Middle Chinese borrowing (MC 'wanX).
トップ is borrowed from English “top”, a doublet of トップス.
膝, “knee, lap”, is from Old Japanese, from Proto-Japonic *pinsa.
インク, “ink”, is borrowed from English, and it supplanted an earlier インキ from Dutch “inkt”.
ジャム is the English word “jam” in katakana.
In 短編, the source says 編 is a daiyōji replacing 篇.
ストレス is borrowed from English “stress”.
また is from Old Japanese and first cited to the Nihon Shoki of 720 CE.
テーマ comes from German “Thema”, first cited in a text from 1910.
生まれる is the passive form of 生む (umu, “to give birth to”), hence “to be born”.
コーチ is borrowed from English “coach”.
ワンピース, “one-piece dress”, is borrowed from English “one-piece”.
切れ is the nominative form of 切れる (kireru, “be cut off, be injured”).
ロッカー is borrowed from English “locker”.
挟む appears to be the Old Japanese root pasa plus the verb-forming suffix む (mu).
ピストル is the English word “pistol” in katakana.
度, “counter for occurrences”, is cognate with 旅 (tabi, “journey, travel”).
フィルム is the English word “film” in katakana.
飾り, “decoration”, is the continuative stem of the verb 飾る (kazaru, “to decorate, to adorn”).
ブラシ is the English word “brush” in katakana.
コーラス is the English word “chorus” in katakana.
建つ, “to stand; to be built”, is cognate with 立つ (tatsu).
テープ is the English word “tape” in katakana.
分かれる comes from the classical verb わかる, and is cognate with 別れる and 分ける.
カーブ covers “curve” and the baseball curve ball, and the source traces it to English “curve”.
写す, “to copy; to photograph”, is cognate with 移す.
カーテン is borrowed from English “curtain”.
